title: Feuerbach's Theorem: Wiedijk #29
content: Feuerbach's Theorem (1822): the nine-point circle of any triangle is internally tangent to the incircle and externally tangent to all three excircles. The nine-point circle passes through 9 special points: midpoints of the three sides, feet of the three altitudes, and midpoints of segments from vertices to the orthocenter. Its radius is $R/2$ (half the circumradius) and its center $N$ is the midpoint of the orthocenter $H$ and circumcenter $O$.
mathContext: The nine-point circle $(N, R/2)$ satisfies $d(N, I) = |R/2 - r|$ (internal tangency with incircle) and $d(N, I_k) = R/2 + r_k$ (external tangency with each excircle $k \in \{a,b,c\}$). The tangent point with the incircle is the Feuerbach point $F$.

title: Triangle Configuration in R²
content: Defines a non-degenerate triangle in $\mathbb{R}^2$ via three vertices $A$, $B$, $C$ with a non-degeneracy condition ensuring positive area. Side lengths $a = |BC|$, $b = |CA|$, $c = |AB|$ are computed via the distance formula, the semi-perimeter $s = (a+b+c)/2$, and the area via the shoelace formula.
mathContext: Non-degeneracy: $(B_x - A_x)(C_y - A_y) - (C_x - A_x)(B_y - A_y) \neq 0$, which is the signed area being nonzero. The shoelace formula gives $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}|\det\begin{pmatrix} B-A \\ C-A \end{pmatrix}|$.

title: Triangle Special Points
content: Defines the circumcenter $O$ (equidistant from all vertices, computed via perpendicular bisector intersection), the circumradius $R = d(O, A)$, the orthocenter $H$ (intersection of altitudes, computed via $H = A + B + C - 2O$), and the centroid $G = (A+B+C)/3$. These three points lie on the Euler line.
mathContext: The Euler line relation: $G = \frac{O + 2H}{3}$, so $G$ divides $\overline{OH}$ in the ratio $1:2$ from $O$. The circumcenter formula uses the system of equations $|OA|^2 = |OB|^2 = |OC|^2$ solved explicitly in coordinates.

title: Nine-Point Circle
content: The nine-point circle has center $N = \frac{O+H}{2}$ (midpoint of circumcenter and orthocenter) and radius $R_9 = R/2$. Also defines the three Euler points: midpoints of $AH$, $BH$, $CH$ (segments from vertices to orthocenter). Together with the three side midpoints and three altitude feet, these give the 9 points on the circle.
mathContext: The nine-point center $N = \frac{O + H}{2}$ lies on the Euler line, midway between $O$ and $H$. The radius $R_9 = R/2$ is proved as a definitional equality. The circle is also called the Euler circle, medioscribed circle, or Feuerbach circle.

title: Incircle and Excircles
content: The incircle has center $I$ (incenter, the intersection of angle bisectors) and inradius $r = \text{Area}/s$. The three excircles have centers $I_a$, $I_b$, $I_c$ (computed via signed barycentric coordinates) and exradii $r_k = \text{Area}/(s - k)$. The incenter uses positive weights $a:b:c$; the excenter $I_a$ uses weights $-a:b:c$.
mathContext: $I = \frac{aA + bB + cC}{a+b+c}$, $r = \frac{\Delta}{s}$. For the excircle opposite $A$: $I_a = \frac{-aA + bB + cC}{-a+b+c}$, $r_a = \frac{\Delta}{s-a}$. The product of all four radii satisfies $r \cdot r_a \cdot r_b \cdot r_c = \Delta^2$.

title: Circle Tangency Conditions
content: Formalizes internal and external tangency between circles. Two circles with centers $c_1$, $c_2$ and radii $r_1$, $r_2$ are internally tangent if $d(c_1, c_2) = |r_1 - r_2|$ (one inside the other, touching at one point) and externally tangent if $d(c_1, c_2) = r_1 + r_2$ (disjoint interiors, touching at one point).
mathContext: Internal tangency: $d(c_1, c_2) = |r_1 - r_2|$ means the circles touch at exactly one point, with the smaller circle inside the larger. External tangency: $d(c_1, c_2) = r_1 + r_2$ means the circles touch at exactly one point, each outside the other.

title: Euler Line Relations (Proved)
content: Two fully proved theorems: (1) the Euler line relation $G = (O + 2H)/3$, proved by coordinate computation with `ring`; (2) the nine-point center lies on the Euler line as the midpoint of $O$ and $H$, proved by reflexivity. These are among the few non-axiom results in the file.
mathContext: The Euler line theorem (Euler, 1767): $O$, $G$, $H$ are collinear with $\overrightarrow{OG} = \frac{1}{3}\overrightarrow{OH}$. Equivalently, $G = \frac{1}{3}O + \frac{2}{3}H$. The nine-point center is $N = \frac{1}{2}(O + H)$.

title: Key Distance Relations (Axiomatized)
content: The core of Feuerbach's theorem: four axiomatized distance relations. (1) $d(N, I) = |R/2 - r|$ establishes internal tangency with the incircle. (2-4) $d(N, I_k) = R/2 + r_k$ for $k \in \{a,b,c\}$ establishes external tangency with each excircle. These are axiomatized because the coordinate-geometry proof requires extensive algebraic manipulation.
mathContext: The Feuerbach distance formula: $NI^2 = R(R - 2r)/4$ where $N$ is the nine-point center, $I$ the incenter. Since $NI = |R/2 - r|$ and $R_9 = R/2$, this gives $NI = |R_9 - r|$, the internal tangency condition. The classical proof uses Euler's identity $OI^2 = R^2 - 2Rr$.

title: Nine-Point Circle Properties (Axiomatized)
content: Six axioms asserting that specific points lie on the nine-point circle: the three side midpoints $M_a$, $M_b$, $M_c$ and the three Euler points (midpoints of $AH$, $BH$, $CH$). Each states $d(N, P) = R/2$. The altitude feet are not separately axiomatized but also lie on this circle.
mathContext: For each of the 9 points $P_i$: $d(N, P_i) = R_9 = R/2$. The proof that side midpoints lie on the nine-point circle follows from $N = (O+H)/2$ and $M_a = (B+C)/2$: the midpoint theorem in the medial triangle shows $NM_a = R/2$.

title: Feuerbach's Theorem: Complete Statement
content: The complete theorem combining all four tangency results into a single conjunction: the nine-point circle is (1) internally tangent to the incircle ($d(N,I) = |R/2 - r|$) and (2-4) externally tangent to each excircle ($d(N,I_k) = R/2 + r_k$). Each part follows directly from the corresponding axiomatized distance relation. The tangent point with the incircle is the Feuerbach point $F$.
mathContext: The full statement: $d(N,I) = |R_9 - r| \wedge \bigwedge_{k \in \{a,b,c\}} d(N, I_k) = R_9 + r_k$. This is Wiedijk's Theorem #29. The proof is a 4-tuple of the distance axioms.

title: Equilateral Triangle Special Case
content: For an equilateral triangle with side $s$: $R = s\sqrt{3}/3$ and $r = s\sqrt{3}/6$, so $R = 2r$. This means $R/2 = r$, so the nine-point circle and incircle have the same radius and are concentric — they coincide. The internal tangency degenerates to coincidence. Axiomatized because the proof requires extensive real arithmetic with $\sqrt{3}$.
mathContext: For an equilateral triangle: $R = 2r$, $R_9 = R/2 = r$, and $N = I$ (all centers coincide). The Feuerbach tangency becomes $d(N,I) = |r - r| = 0$, confirming coincidence. The equilateral triangle is the unique triangle where all excircles have equal radii: $r_a = r_b = r_c$.

title: Numerical Verification: 3-4-5 Right Triangle
content: Concrete verification with the 3-4-5 right triangle ($A = (0,0)$, $B = (3,0)$, $C = (0,4)$). Three fully proved results: area $= 6$, semi-perimeter $= 6$, inradius $= 1$. The side lengths are computed via $\sqrt{9+16} = 5$, $\sqrt{16} = 4$, $\sqrt{9} = 3$ using `Real.sqrt_eq_iff_sq_eq`.
mathContext: For the 3-4-5 triangle: $a = 5$, $b = 4$, $c = 3$, $s = 6$, $\Delta = 6$, $r = 1$, $R = 5/2$ (circumradius equals half the hypotenuse for right triangles), $R_9 = 5/4$. The Feuerbach distance is $|R/2 - r| = |5/4 - 1| = 1/4$.
